recipes.name: Mexican Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes with juice

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef, and stir in the taco seasoning and tomatoes. Line a 9x13-inch baking dish with half the tortillas. Spoon the beef mixture into the dish, then top with the remaining tortillas. Spread salsa over the tortillas and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 20 to 30 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: My whole family loves this beefy lasagna flavored with taco seasoning. Even my picky five-year-old will eat it. Serve with shredded lettuce, fresh sliced tomatoes, olives and sour cream.

review.reviewBody:
Delicious and easy! Here are my changes. 1. Grease the pan with cooking spray. 2. Spread refried beans on 1st layer of tortillas. 3. Used chopped fresh tomatoes rather than canned. 4. Added an extra layer...tortillas/beans& beef, cheese & salsa, tortillas, beef, tortillas, taco sauce and cheese.
Really good with some sour cream and/or hot sauce on the side!

Yum Yum Yummmmmmmmy. This was easy to make and delicious. I did lightly coat the pan to keep things from sticking. I put refried beans on top of the first layer of tortillas. In the meat, I added onions and some garlic powder. I used more like 2 cups of cheese but I also added more layers. My layers went like this: Tortilla, refried beans, beef mixture, cheese, tortilla, beef mixture, cheese, tortilla, salsa and a lil more cheese. My mom and grandma tried it at lunch today and loved it as well. I served it with sour cream. The only thing I would do different next time is use 1 1/2 lb of hamburger. I think with the extra layer I needed a bit more.

This is a great start to a fantastic recipe. It needs a few additions, though. For a group of 8 adults, I doubled the recipe. Spray the pan as recommended by others. I also suggest quartering the corn tortillas as it made cutting, serving and eating less messy and kept the serving sizes more intact and pretty on the plate. Additionally, I added 2 cans of refried beans on top of the first layer of tortillas, 1 can of corn, 2 cans green enchilada sauce poured over the last layer but before the cheese topping, 2 zucchini chopped and sauteed with the hamburger when the hamburger was almost fully cooked, 1 can of Rotel tomatoes, 2 cans diced green chilis, 1 can sliced black olives on top of the last layer of cheese. It was the perfect ratio for everything. It wasn't too runny or dry. Just perfect! Keep any eye on the cheese topping and cover with foil if needed to keep it from burning. Garnished with chopped cilantro and green onions. It was a hit with everyone they they all asked for the recipe. We even had leftovers for the next day and kept the party train going.

To serve 4, I sautéed onions with 3/4 lb. ground turkey, mixing in 1/2 env. low-sodium Taco seasoning plus one can green enchilada sauce and 1/2 can Rotel tomatoes. Then added 1/2 can pinto beans. I sprayed Pam on a 2 1/2 qt. Oval baking dish before placing 3 corn tortillas on the bottom. Then layered 1/2 meat mixture. Next layer was a mix of 1 cup ricotta cheese, 1 egg and 1/2 cup Mexican cheese. Repeated tortillas, meat mixture and finally more cheese. Spread sliced black olives on top, then baked 30 min. at 350 degrees. Hubby loved it.

My family is ecstatic every time I make this! I make a vegetarian version using tofu crumbles instead of ground beef. It is seriously delicious and meat eaters never even realize the difference. Here are my changes and layers:
1. spinach tortillas from Whole Foods bakery. seriously do it.
2. i fold the tortillas in half and tear them, flat side facing out
3. i use wax paper to line the pan
4. 1st layer tortillas
5. 2nd layer Rosita's veggie refried beans
6. Boca crumbles (seasoned just like the beef with McKormick's original taco seasoning in a skillet first)
7. Mateo's medium salsa
8. Shredded mexican cheese (sargento)
9. 2nd layer tortillas
10. more beans
11. rest of boca crumbles
12. cheese
13. 3rd layer tortillas
14. rest of 1 can of beans
15. salsa
16. fresh cilantro spread out
17. sliced jalapeno's
18. rest of cheese

It bakes perfectly in 20-25 minutes, and if you make some guacamole on the side that is all you need to make this meal perfecto!! Muchas gracias for the base recipe idea!!!

I made this tonight with just a couple changes:
1) browned ground beef, drained then added diced tomatoes, chopped onion, minced garlic, chopped jalapeño and taco seasoning. 
2) sprayed cooking pan with non stick spray
3) laid flour tortillas topped with re fried beans, then meat mixture then shredded cheddar and mozzarella cheese, another layer just like this, then a layer of tortilla shells topped with salsa and shredded cheeses and black olives. 
4) baked 350 for 25 minutes

It was good but nothing over the top, certainly glad I added the jalapeño, garlic, onion and tomatoes to meat mixture or this would have been very bland.

You can cut the round tortilla shells in half to fit the pan on the sides better and place the round ones in the middle. I make more layers by warming refried beans and spreading this over a layer of tortilla shells and topping with shredded cheddar cheese and another layer of Spanish Rice spread over a layer of tortilla shells and sprinkling with more cheese. I buy a huge foil roasing pan so you don't have to worry about this rising over the dish while baking, let it rest after it's done, cut a square and top with shredded lettuce, black olives, diced fresh tomatoes, diced green onion and top with sour cream, taco sauce, warmed jarred mexican cheese sauce poured over all....a masterpiece.

So....family did like this recipe. However, I think it could have used a bit more sauce, like a regular lasagna. We will definitely be making again, flavors are good. I did make some changes: used lasagna noodles, because hubby just didn't want it with corn tortillas. I added a layer of cheese over meat, a blend of ricotta, sour cream, cilantro, mexican blend shredded and salsa). Like I said, we will definitely make again, and I will do the corn tortillas for myself next time (I also have to modify with a veggie sub for meat, due to vegetarian) but I am looking forward to it. Thanks!

Easy weeknight meal! I have made this several times and am just barely getting around to reviewing it. I took the suggestion of other reviewers by spraying the baking dish with cooking spray, spreading a layer of refried beans on the first layer of tortillas plus adding more layers and more cheese. I also replaced the diced tomatoes with canned green chiles because having diced tomatoes and salsa would be too much tomato for me. Served with Mexican Rice on the side and sour cream & hot sauce on top!

I made this for dinner last night and my boyfriend really enjoyed it. I took some suggestions and added a few extra touches. 
1) I used corn tortillas. I sprayed the bottom of the dish with cooking spray and then later 6 small tortillas down. 
2) Next I spread half a can of refried beans on the tortillas. 
3) Third I took half my ground turkey mixture (I added a small diced onion and next time I may try some garlic and diced jalopanos as well) on top of the refried beans and then I sprinkled a half a cup of cheese over that. 
4) I added the second layer of tortillas, the second layer of the ground turkey mixture and then I drizzled that layer with taco sauce. 
5) Finally I added the last layer of tortillas as well as the salsa and almost 2 cups of cheese. (We use lowfat cheese so a little extra won't hurt). 

The end result was amazing. I used a little sour cream and my boyfriend used some salsa. We both had enough for lunch the next day and leftovers for a night from now!

Loved it! I am a casserole person. This was quick and easy. I used two lbs of ground beef, 2 pkgs taco seasoning, 1 can spicy refried beans, 1 can of rotel and 1 can of mexi-style corn and flour tortilla. I slathered 1/2 of the beans on 2 of the flour tortillas and put them on the bottom of the greased 4.5 x 9 casserole dish. browned the meat with peppers (red & jalepeno) and onion, drained the fat off, added the taco seasonings, the rotel, a cup of water and the drained corn until heated through. They I layered 1/2 the ground beef mix on top of the tortillas and beans. added another layer of tortillas and beans the rest of the ground beef mix and then topped with cheese. backed for .5 hour at 375 degrees. Now while the changes I made do make some difference it should not be as much as you would think. Anyway we loved it! Thanks for the recipe, definitely a keeper.
The original recipe is absolutely delicious, but reading the “changes” on this one like I always do, OMG! Some people wandered so far away, you scare me!

I've made this for over 20 years. Scratch the taco seasoning...to the meat I add cumin, oregano, garlic powder and onion powder. After adding tomatoes, add 1/2 cup chopped cilantro then put in dish. Created 2nd layer with fresh or frozen corn (heated) then spread on 3/4 c salsa. Add another layer of tortillas, then salsa and cheese. I spritz all tortillas lightly with avocado oil. Serve with sour cream. Delish!
Awesome recipe... Took a few to get everything together,but well worth the effort. Very Yummy Too!
Added refried beans like most reviewers. Also did a small amount of salsa con queso dip in between a layer.

This was yummy! My family loved it. Added some refried beans over the tortillas. I didn’t have the diced tomatoes and used tomato sauce in place. It was fantastic! Will definitely add to the recipe box.
Great recipe! I also sliced a big beefsteak tomato and laid the slices on the meat, covered in tortilla chips, then salsa & cheese. Baked a little longer and was fabulous!

This was very good. I am going to make it again but increase the ingredients by at least half as it was "thin" but tasty. It needs either a smaller pan or increased amounts to get a truer "lasagna" result. Circling the plate with shredded lettuce & diced tomatoes make a lovely presentation.
tasty used hot salsa
Delish! My family loved it. I did add a layer of refried beans to it, but other than that it was perfect. It's a keepie!
